ORAL COMMUNICATIONS / POSSIBLE DIRECTION TO STAFF (30 MINUTES)
Each speaker is allowed three (3) minutes to address the City Council. Time donations are not permitted during Oral Communications. Please submit a â€œWHITEâ€ speaker slip to the City Clerk. If at least two (2) Council Members agree, direction may be given to staff to put an item on a future agenda or provide additional information to answer a question.
7.
CHANGES TO THE AGENDA Announcements of administrative changes to the agenda, in compliance with the Brown Act.
The title of ordinances listed on this agenda are deemed to have been read and further reading waived.
8.
CONSENT CALENDAR The recommendations on the following Consent Calendar will be enacted in one motion unless an item is removed from the Calendar. Any member of the public may remove an item by submitting a â€œPINKâ€ speaker slip to the City Clerk. Items removed from the Consent Calendar by a Council Member or the public will be considered immediately following the Consent Calendar.
If a public hearing item is part of the consent calendar, the public hearing shall be deemed held if the item is not removed from the consent calendar for discussion and possible action.
8A.
Approval of the Minutes of the February 14, 2018 Closed Session, February 14, 2018 Special Meeting and February 14, 2018 Regular Meeting. Contact Person: City Clerk Hollywood
Approve the Minutes.
2018-03-14 Item 08A Minutes
8B.
Approval of the Warrants List. Contact Person: Finance Manager Lundgren
Approve the Warrants.
2018-03-14 Item 08B Warrants
8C.
Cancelation of the March 28, 2018 Regular City Council meeting. Contact Person: City Clerk Hollywood
Council approve canceling the March 28, 2018 Regular City Council meeting.
2018-03-14 Item 08C Cancelation of March 28 Regular Meeting
8D.
Appointments to the Commission for the Arts, Environmental Commission, Parks and Recreation Commission, Senior Citizen Commission and Traffic & Public Safety Commission. Contact Person: City Clerk Hollywood
Council to approve: 1) the Mayor's recommendations for appointments to the Environmental Commission, Parks and Recreation Commission, Senior Citizen Commission and Traffic & Public Safety Commission; and 2) the Deputy Mayor's recommendations for appointments to the Commission for the Arts.
2018-03-14 Item 08D Commission Appointments
8E.
The Preparation and Filing of the Encinitas Landscape and Lighting District Annual Report. Contact Person: Senior Management Analyst Ruess
Adopt City Council Resolution No. 2018-08 entitled, â€œResolution of the City Council of the City of Encinitas Directing the Preparation and Filing of the Encinitas Landscape and Lighting District Annual Report for the Purposes of Levying and Collecting Assessments for Fiscal Year 2018-19.
2018-03-14 Item 08E Encinitas Landscaping and Lighting District Annual Report
8F.
Emergency Declaration Memorandum in response to the abandoned vessel south of Beaconâ€™s Beach and budget amendment Resolution 2018-29. Contact Person: Fire Chief Stein
1) Receive the Emergency Declaration Memorandum dated February 13, 2018; and 2) Approve Resolution 2018-29 for a budget amendment of $14,500 to the Marine Safety Division budget.
2018-03-14 Item 08F Emergency Declaration Abandoned Vessel
8G.
Mobile Data Computer (MDC) Replacement. Contact Person: Deputy Fire Chief Blumeyer
City Council takes the following actions: 1) Approve the request of Capital Equipment Replacement funds held by North County Dispatch Joint Powers Authority (NCDJPA); 2) Approve the contract with CDCE, Incorporated for the purchase and installation of 12 Mobile Data Computers for emergency vehicles; and 3) Adopt City Council Resolution No. 2018-25 amending the FY 2017-18 operating budget to accept General Fund revenue of $73,824 and increase the budget appropriations in the General Fund by $73,824 and the County Service Area-17 Fund by $18,603 for the purchase and installation of the equipment.
2018-03-14 Item 08G Resolution 2018-25 Budget Adjustment & Mobile Data Computer Replacements
8H.
Pilot North County Coastal Regional Bikeshare Program. Contact Person: CAP Program Administrator
It is recommended that the City Council take the following actions: 1) Authorize the City Manager, or designee, of the City of Encinitas to enter into a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the cities of Del Mar, Solana Beach, Carlsbad, and Oceanside, as well as Camp Pendleton and North County Transit District (NCTD) to develop and implement a one-year pilot regional bikeshare program; 2) Authorize the City of Encinitas to serve as the lead jurisdiction; and 3) Authorize City staff to issue a Request for Information (RFI) to seek proposals from vendors with the resources to pilot a bikeshare program.
2018-03-14 Item 08H Regional Bikeshare Memorandum of Understanding
8I.
License Agreement between the City and the Friends of the Encinitas Library regarding the use and utilization of space at the Encinitas Community Library. Contact Person: Senior Management Analyst McSeveney
Approve entering into a renewed license agreement with the Friends of the Encinitas Library (â€œFriendsâ€) for the utilization of the 750 square foot storefront space at the Encinitas Community Library, and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement.
2018-03-14 Item 08I Friends of Library License Agreement 2018
8J.
Moonlight State Beach Concession License Agreement. Contact Person: Management Analyst Roff
City Council take the following actions: 1) Approve the Moonlight State Beach Concession License Agreement in substantial form; and 2) Authorize the City Manager in conjunction with the City Attorney to execute the Moonlight State Beach Concession License Agreement with Aqua Nutracueticals for three years commencing upon the date of execution by the parties with an option to extend, upon mutual consent, for two additional one-year terms.
2018-03-14 Item 08J Moonlight Beach Concession Agreement
8K.
Mobility Project Update - Capital Improvement and Traffic Engineering Divisions. Contact Person: City Engineer Magdosku
Receive the report on the status of Capital Improvement and Traffic Engineering projects; and provide direction if necessary and appropriate.
2018-03-14 Item 08K Mobility Projects Update
8L.
Second reading and adoption of two City Council Ordinances No. 2018-01 and No. 2018-02, which propose changes to Title 30 (Zoning) of the Encinitas Municipal Code to define Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) and Junior Accessory Dwelling Units (JADUs), respectively, and establishes development standards for these units based on recent updates to State Law. The proposed ordinances will amend the Cityâ€™s zoning regulations and Local Coastal Program. CASE NO: 16-25 ZA/LCPA; LOCATION: Citywide. Contact Person: Associate Planner Plagemann
1) Adopt City Council Ordinance No. 2018-01 titled, â€œAn Ordinance of the City Council of the City of Encinitas, California, adopting amendments to Title 30 (Zoning) of the Encinitas Municipal Code to address changes in state law regarding accessory dwelling units,â€ as reflected in Attachment CC-1 for the reasons specified in the Agenda Report; and 2) Adopt City Council Ordinance No. 2018-02 titled, â€œAn Ordinance of the City Council of the City of Encinitas, California, adopting amendments to Title 30 (Zoning) of the Encinitas Municipal Code to address state law regarding junior accessory dwelling units,â€ as reflected in Attachment CC-2 for the reasons specified in the Agenda Report.
2018-03-14 Item 08L ADU-JADU Second Reading and Adoption of Ordinances 2018-01 and 2018-02
9.
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR Staff reports will be given only if requested by the person who pulled the item.
PROCEDURES FOR PUBLIC HEARINGS ON APPEALS (ITEMS 10A and 10B): New information such as documents, exhibits, letters, photos, charts, diagrams, videos, etc., WILL NOT be considered by the City Council if presented at this meeting. All material must have been submitted to the City Clerk no less than 7 calendar days prior to this hearing.
10.
ACTION ITEMS
10A.
Public hearing to consider an appeal of the Development Services Directorâ€™s approval of a Coastal Development Permit to convert an existing lower level crawl space, approximately 350 square feet in size, into habitable area, add 55 square feet to the upstairs bedroom, and add a small deck to an attached single-family residence. CASE NUMBER: 17-159 CDP; APPLICANT: Robby Fender, GCA, LLC; APPELLANT: Darlene Jacobsen; LOCATION: 1704 Tattenham Road (APN: 254-540-13). Contact Person: Associate Planner Halverson
Deny the appeal, and adopt Draft Resolution No. 2018-16 affirming the decision of the Development Services Director in approving the Coastal Development Permit to allow the conversion of a lower level crawl space into habitable area, add 55 square feet to the upstairs bedroom, and add a small deck to an attached single-family residence.
2018-03-14 Item 10A Public Hearing to Consider an Appeal 17-159 Located at 1704 Tattenham Road
10B.
Continued Public Hearing to consider two timely-filed appeals of the Planning Commission's approval of the Westmont of Encinitas Assisted Living facility. The project site is located within the Residential 3 (R-3) Zone and the Coastal Zone in the community of New Encinitas. CASE NUMBER: 16-131 MUP/DR/PMW/EIA/CDP; APPLICANT: Richard Lux/Westmont Development, LLC; APPELLANT NO. 1: Linda Lux; APPELLANT NO. 2: Marilyn Dulich, Robert Denyer, Shaun Cornell, Kelli Cornell, Richard Markell, Kristen Markell, Dan Lowe, Dana Lowe, Linda Lux and Bobby Lux as members of the Encinitas Citizens for Responsible, Respectful Encinitas Development; LOCATION: 252 North El Camino Real (APN: 262-160-26 and -27). Contact Person: Associate Planner Mierau
Option A Deny both appeals, uphold the approval of the Planning Commission decision and adopt the attached draft City Council Resolution 2018-14.
2018-03-14 Item 10B Westmont Appeal - PART 1 (Pages 1- 417)
2018-03-14 Item 10B Westmont Appeal - PART 2 (Pages 418-677)
10C.
Presentation, discussion and development of a refined implementation strategy for establishing a Quiet Zone within the Encinitas rail corridor. Contact Person: Associate Civil Engineer Kellar
Provide staff with direction to pursue a Quiet Zone implementation strategy.
2018-03-14 Item 10C Quiet Zone Within the Encinitas Rail Corridor
10D.
Preliminary zero emission vehicle (ZEV) fleet conversion plan, authorization to install Power Your Drive Charging Stations at the Public Works yard, purchase of fleet vehicles due for replacement in FY 2017-18, and acceptance of donation for the Marine Safety Bicycles. Contact Person: CAP Program Administrator Najera and Senior Analyst Wilson
It is recommended that the City Council take the following action: 1. Receive the preliminary zero emission vehicle (ZEV) fleet conversion plan (Attachment 1); 2. Authorize the City Manager, or designee, to enter into a license agreement, in substantial form, as attached hereto, subject to final review and approval of City Attorney, with SDG&E for the installation of ten (10) Power Your Drive Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Stations to be installed at the Public Works yard (Attachment 2); 3. Authorize the use of funding from the Facilities Fund to pay for the City's portion of the installation cost for the Power Your Drive EV Charging Stations, in the amount of $11,800, and pay for upgrading three (3) existing Level 1 EV charging stations at City Hall to Level 2 EV charging stations, in the amount of $5,500; 4. Ratify the purchase of the described vehicles from National Joint Powers Alliance (NJPA) in accordance with the attached quotes, for an amount not-to-exceed $295,000 plus up-fit costs not to exceed $180,000 for a total amount of $475,000, to cover purchases in FY 2017-18 (Attachment 3); 5. Authorize staff to apply for any applicable rebates that the City is eligible to receive for the purchase of zero and/or low emission vehicles; and 6. Accept the donation of two (2) bicycles from Electra Bicycle Company for the exclusive use of the Marine Safety Division to reduce vehicle mileage for non-emergency trips made by lifeguard personnel (Attachment 4).
2018-03-14 Item 10D FY17-18 Fleet Replacement

Notice to the Public:
To ensure that the City meets your needs when addressing the City Council, all presentation materials which require the use of visual equipment need to be submitted to the City's IT Division at least 24 hours in advance of the meeting (except for appeal hearings where materials must be submitted 7 days in advance). This includes photographs, Microsoft Office documents (PowerPoint, Word, Excel). No CD's, DVD's, or USB thumb/flash drives will be accepted at the meeting. All materials must be in PC format and digital presentation items must be emailed to it-service-desk@encinitasca.gov . Please label all materials with the corresponding agenda item number. Should technical assistance be necessary, it will be available to presenters from 5:30 p.m. to 5:50 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Presentation of video/digital/photographs are considered part of the maximum time limit provided to speakers.
